incident-bot: PAGER: on-call SRE Maya paged for high gpu.driver.reset rate on inference-cluster-us-east-1. Severity: P1. Alert: gpu.driver.reset.count > 3 in 2m. https://infra/alerts/2945007777
Maya: ack — jumping in. I can repro driver resets on node-gpu-27, seeing repeating Xid 61 entries and ECC correctable spikes.
SRE-Lisa: I’m in the logs. Kernel shows repeated `NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 61` followed by `oom-killer` on some inference containers.
Ryan: tagging @Maya @SRE-Lisa — this just started ~2m ago after a batch job rolled out on dedicated-capacity-2? Could be a noisy kernel module.
Maya: Verified: pod inference-serve-abc restarting with OOM + container crash. Latency/5xxs on hosted API increased ~18% for the past 3 mins.
Jon: Putting node-gpu-27 into cordon to stop new pods: `kubectl cordon node-gpu-27`.
Maya: running drain now with ignore-daemonsets, preserving PDBs: `kubectl drain node-gpu-27 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=5m`
Trevor: I'm ramping up fallback routing on the API gateway to route 30% to dedicated-failover region to reduce customer impact.
Cust-Bridge-Bot: Started customer bridge for impacted customers. Notifying top 3 customers with active inferences.
SRE-Lisa: Posting relevant log snippet: ```
May 05 12:04:11 node-gpu-27 kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 61, pid=2345, thread_name=python, gfx=0 506.98, UUID=...
May 05 12:04:12 node-gpu-27 kernel: gpu ecc: correctable error count 287 -> 312
May 05 12:04:13 node-gpu-27 kubelet: oom-kill event for container inference-serve-abc: killed process 2345 (python) total-vm: 12G, anon-rss: 5.6G
```
Ryan: This pattern looks like an ECC-correctable escalation leading to driver resets under load. Could be thermal or a bad DIMM but starting with driver restart and telemetry capture is fastest.
Maya: Agreed. Ops runbook step: restart nvidia driver on node-gpu-27 and collect dmesg + nv-smi telemetry. Running: `sudo systemctl restart nvidia-driver.service` now.
Jon: Before restart, I snapshot telemetry: `nv-smi --query-gpu=temperature.gpu,utilization.gpu,memory.used --format=csv` -> temp=88C util=98% mem=11.9GB. High temp but within limit.
SRE-Lisa: After restart we saw Xid count spike then a drop. Driver restart logs: `nvidia: resetting GPU` then `nvidia: driver reloaded`. But process OOMs persisted on some pods.
Maya: I’m evicting remaining inference pods from the node and will leave node cordoned for evaluation. Creating a quarantine label: `kubectl label node node-gpu-27 quarantine=investigating`
Trevor: Noting impact: 12 pods evicted, approximate capacity loss ~18% on the cluster. Serving latency now back to baseline for routed traffic but overall request rate slightly degraded.
Cust-Bridge-Bot: Customer update drafted: "We're investigating GPU instability causing transient failures in inference; engineering is actively mitigating with node quarantine and fallbacks. We'll update in 30 minutes."
Ryan: Opening a deeper triage: snapshot of ECC counters across fleet shows node-gpu-27 ECC correctables at 320 vs fleet median 4. Next step: schedule hardware test and live kernel oops repro.
SRE-Lisa: Created post-incident ticket INFR-9421 and attached logs + nv-smi dumps. Keeping node quarantined until hardware swap or DIMM re-seat.
Maya: Oncall handoff in 30m — @Trevor will take second-shift. Leaving runbook actions: 1) maintain cordon, 2) collect cross-node ECC trends (`/opt/telemetry/ecc_rollup.sh`), 3) keep customer bridge updated.
Trevor: Ack — I'll own the bridge and follow up with a hardware escalation if ECC counters don't drop after coldboot. Also will validate model fallback config for reduced failure blast radius.
Jon: Quick mitigation note for others: if you see Xid 61 + OOM pattern, prefer draining node and routing to failover rather than immediate driver reload if customers are impacted. Driver restart is noisy.
SRE-Lisa: Adding that to runbook doc with sample commands and thresholds.
Maya: Closing temporary incident channel: moving to postmortem once hardware validation done. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: status -> mitigated (traffic routed; node cordoned); next update scheduled in 30m.
